advances: The three simultaneous common-upper Brunn--Minkowski inequalities, the complete endpoint Venn atom identities, the exact endpoint-family cover alternative, and the full residual area constraints do not imply the global row target.  The exact rational joint cell survivor below isolates the missing actual-body datum: the three same-index midpoint-pullback chain graphs and their vertex covers.
author: mp_r253_common_upper_closure
proof:
All displayed cells are nonnegative.  Their row sums are
\[
\frac34+3\left(\frac1{12}\right)=1,\qquad
3\left(\frac1{27}\right)=\frac19,\qquad
3\left(\frac13\right)=1,
\]
so they give the asserted three slice areas.  Because the cells form disjoint membership partitions, they encode every union and intersection identity of the three caps on each endpoint, not merely the six cap marginals.  Explicitly, all pairwise and triple cap intersections have area zero, and
\[
x_i=\frac1{12},\qquad y_i=\frac1{27},\qquad
e_i=x_i+y_i=\frac{13}{108}.
\tag{1}
\]
The exact common-upper identities give, simultaneously for all \(k\),
\[
u_{0k}=d_{0,\varnothing}+d_{0,\{k\}}
=\frac34+\frac1{12}=\frac56,
\qquad
u_{2k}=d_{2,\varnothing}+d_{2,\{k\}}
=\frac1{27}.
\tag{2}
\]

The smaller endpoint is covered with multiplicity one almost everywhere:
\[
d_{2,\varnothing}=0,\qquad
A_2=C_{21}\cup C_{22}\cup C_{23}\quad\text{at the level of the complete Venn table},
\qquad
\sum_i y_i=\frac19=a_2.
\tag{3}
\]
This is exactly the second endpoint alternative of accepted fact `0b5d84877f51b7c3`.  It also implies its product cover, weighted payment, and total endpoint payment:
\[
\sum_i\left(\frac{x_i}{a_0}+\frac{y_i}{a_2}\right)
=\frac14+1=\frac54\ge1,
\qquad
\sum_i e_i=\frac{13}{36}\ge\frac19=\min\{a_0,a_2\}.
\tag{4}
\]

The constant-sum sign restrictions are also retained rather than projected away.  With \(\sum_i s_i=-2\), the three slice-\(0\) affine expressions have sum
\[
\sum_i(f_i-s_i)=-1-\sum_i s_i=1,
\]
so the all-cap cell is forbidden; indeed \(d_{0,I}=0\).  The three slice-\(2\) expressions have sum
\[
\sum_i(f_i+s_i)=-1+\sum_i s_i=-3,
\]
so the all-strict-upper cell is forbidden; indeed \(d_{2,\varnothing}=0\).  In the middle slice, \(\sum_i f_i=-1\) forbids the all-strict-upper cell; indeed \(d_{1,\varnothing}=0\).  Moreover, the middle cells give
\[
b_i=\frac13,\qquad \sum_i b_i=1=a_1,
\tag{5}
\]
so the three \(B_i\) cover the middle slice with multiplicity one almost everywhere.  These are precisely the incidence consequences of the normalized strict three-row form supplied by accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0`.

For the residual area audit, \(M=1\), \(m=1/9\), \(r=1/9\), and \(s=1\).  Since \(r\le9/25\), accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e` gives
\[
L(r)=1-r=\frac89,\qquad U(r)=1+r=\frac{10}{9}.
\]
Thus \(L(r)<s<U(r)\), and \(0<r<\rho\) because that fact also gives \(\rho>1/2\).  The compatibility area inequality holds as well:
\[
\frac{(1+\sqrt r)^2}{4}
=\frac{(1+1/3)^2}{4}
=\frac49<1=s.
\tag{6}
\]
Hence the point lies strictly in the full residual area strip.

It remains to check the three square-root cross terms.  Equations (2) and (5) give, for every \(k\),
\[
\left(\sqrt{u_{0k}}+\sqrt{u_{2k}}\right)^2
=\left(\sqrt{\frac56}+\sqrt{\frac1{27}}\right)^2
=\frac{47}{54}+\frac{\sqrt{10}}9.
\]
This is strictly less than \(4/3=4b_k\), because
\[
\frac43-\frac{47}{54}=\frac{25}{54}
>\frac{\sqrt{10}}9
\]
is equivalent, after multiplying by \(54\) and squaring positive quantities, to
\[
25^2>36\cdot10.
\]
Therefore every simultaneous unprojected Brunn--Minkowski inequality from accepted fact `e8452e5481063dd4` holds strictly.

Finally,
\[
T=1+1+\frac19=\frac{19}{9},\qquad
\frac{2T}{9}=\frac{38}{81},
\]
whereas every row has
\[
b_i+e_i=\frac13+\frac{13}{108}
=\frac{49}{108}
=\frac{38}{81}-\frac5{324}
<\frac{2T}{9}.
\tag{7}
\]
This proves the claimed failure of the row target within the complete retained area-incidence system.

The table is deliberately not asserted to come from actual convex bodies and one common affine triple.  The next actual-body condition is the same-index midpoint-pullback condition isolated by accepted fact `a2a1f8532c91018f`: for
\[
E_i=\left\{(u,v)\in A_0\times A_2:
f_i\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)<0\right\},
\]
one must retain simultaneously
\[
E_1\cup E_2\cup E_3=A_0\times A_2
\]
and, for each \(i\),
\[
E_i\subseteq
(C_{0i}\times A_2)\cup(A_0\times C_{2i}).
\tag{8}
\]
The sets \(E_i\) are threshold chain graphs tied together by the same affine functions.  Their vertex-cover numbers satisfy the exact duality in accepted fact `a2a1f8532c91018f`.  One-body Venn tables and the three pairwise common-upper inequalities do not encode the cross-endpoint midpoint incidences in (8).  Thus the next test is the genuinely joint inequality
\[
\max_i\bigl(b_i+\tau(E_i)\bigr)\ge\frac{2T}{9},
\]
not another projection of the endpoint cap cells.
statement:
Let \(I=\{1,2,3\}\).  For \(\ell\in\{0,2\}\) and \(S\subseteq I\), let \(d_{\ell,S}\) denote the measure of the endpoint Venn cell whose points belong to precisely the caps \(C_{\ell i}\) with \(i\in S\).  Thus
\[
a_\ell=\sum_{S\subseteq I}d_{\ell,S},\qquad
x_i=\sum_{S\ni i}d_{0,S},\qquad
y_i=\sum_{S\ni i}d_{2,S},
\]
and, for \(\{i,j,k\}=I\),
\[
u_{\ell k}
=\left|A_\ell\setminus(C_{\ell i}\cup C_{\ell j})\right|
=d_{\ell,\varnothing}+d_{\ell,\{k\}}.
\]
Define middle cells \(d_{1,S}\) in the same way using membership in the three sets \(B_i\), so that
\[
a_1=\sum_{S\subseteq I}d_{1,S},\qquad
b_i=\sum_{S\ni i}d_{1,S}.
\]

There is an exact rational assignment with
\[
a_0=1,\qquad a_1=1,\qquad a_2=\frac19,\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^3s_i=-2,
\]
given, for every \(i\in I\), by
\[
d_{0,\varnothing}=\frac34,\qquad
d_{0,\{i\}}=\frac1{12},
\]
\[
d_{2,\varnothing}=0,\qquad
d_{2,\{i\}}=\frac1{27},
\]
\[
d_{1,\varnothing}=0,\qquad
d_{1,\{i\}}=\frac13,
\]
with every cell of cardinality at least two equal to zero.  It satisfies all endpoint and middle Venn identities, the endpoint-family cover alternative of accepted fact `0b5d84877f51b7c3`, the normalized sign exclusions associated with accepted fact `d2d117bcc58a1ba0`, the full strict residual strip of accepted fact `15bb2c1680a0254e`, and all three unprojected inequalities retained from accepted fact `e8452e5481063dd4`.  Nevertheless,
\[
b_i+x_i+y_i<\frac{2(a_0+a_1+a_2)}9
\qquad(i=1,2,3).
\]
Thus these simultaneous area and incidence data alone do not prove the row target.
